Short description

Save the drama for the screen. With Popcorn Vote, everyone brings a film and gets the same number of votes. Save them, spend them, or switch sides before movie night. The top film wins; a wheel delivers the plot twist when the vote deadlocks. Afterwards, ratings and watched films become a shared family movie diary.

Boilerplate

Popcorn Vote is a free and open-source web app that settles family movie night without a group chat excavation. Everyone brings a film, receives votes on the same schedule, and can save, spend, or move them before the big decision. The top film wins; an animated wheel breaks deadlocks. After the credits, watched films and everyone’s ratings build a shared family movie diary. Popcorn Vote is mobile-first, installable as a PWA, available in nine interface languages, and includes a TV view for the big reveal. It runs as a single Docker container on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 with SQLite storage and no separate database service. It is MIT licensed.

Popcorn Vote — a self-hosted family movie-night voting app

I built a small web app to settle what’s on tonight without excavating a group chat. Everyone brings a film and gets the same number of votes. Save them, spend them, or switch sides before movie night. If the leaders are tied, the wheel makes the final call. Afterwards, watched films and ratings stay in a shared archive.

Software directory

Popcorn Vote is a free, self-hosted app where everyone brings a film, gets the same number of votes, and helps settle what’s on tonight. Votes can be saved, spent, or moved; an animated wheel breaks deadlocks. Watched films and ratings form a shared family movie diary. It runs as one Docker container with SQLite on amd64 and arm64 and is MIT licensed.

A small print, kept small

Usage notes.

Name and positioning

Write the name as “Popcorn Vote”. Describe it as a family project and a self-hosted open-source app, not as a hosted service or commercial product.

Visuals

You may resize the supplied assets while preserving their aspect ratio. Please do not recolour the icon, place text over screenshots, or imply an endorsement.

Third-party artwork

Some screenshots and the demo contain film posters and metadata supplied by TMDB. That third-party content is shown only to demonstrate the app and is not covered by the project's MIT license.

Contact and attribution

Credit “Popcorn Vote by Stadicus” and link to popcornvote.org. For factual corrections or media questions, open an issue in the GitHub repository.
